body:
Design-stage. The working spec is .adlc/specs/58-a-connection-is-a-peer.md, drafted 2026-09-01 from the chat in which Myk named the abstraction and settled its shape. The seam: §27, §28, §39, and §46 all say the container is the primitive and a connection binds to one, while the implementation still grants standing verb by verb at the store entity and binds no container at consent. The section finishes them: an MCP connection is a peer, and the container it binds to is its whole grant.

DECIDED (Myk, in chat): the store root and the user's home container are never bound and never offered to a foreign key (the whole ground travels only to the same operator key); every binding target is at depth two or deeper under the provisioning user; standing derives from the binding (write into its pool, register under its path, federate within its subtree, delegate to its descendants); full leeway inside the subtree with the walls at the edge (no upward writes, no constitution, no code without a person, the envelope, no erasure); posture set at provisioning replaces the grant ladder; names are paths; siblings share by federating and promotion is the person's; migration is a declaration; the offer door serves containers.

Open for Myk's word: self-sever inside the subtree; blessing renderers inside the subtree; the offer-door compatibility window; preset names; whether authorship-on-the-read-surface stays in the arc.

Six slices, each its own landing, ordered so nothing a connection can do today stops working before its replacement lands: S1 bind at consent (home and target provisioned in one act; per-(client, user) key; forward-only inbox; migration by declaration; the Connections panel bind action; reads scoped to the binding); S2 the container tools and derived standing (register under the path with its colon, receive within the subtree, delegation with attenuation and cascade, then the grant verbs retire); S3 the offer token and the container door; S4 the person acts on the page (share-into, promotion with a destination signed as the owner, leeway edits); S5 names and the tree (dissolves T260); S6 authorship on the read surface (T259 second half). 
Acceptance criteria: the working spec's twelve, each naming its rail — see the spec. This design ticket closes when the section lands as spec/58-a-connection-is-a-peer.md with its Provenance footer after S1–S5 have merged.

Review record: spec-lint verified; a Gemini cross-model pass and a three-angle premortem (the person, the substrate, reach and leakage) found seventeen gaps, five blocking; all folded into the spec on 2026-09-01 and named at the positions they changed.
title: §58 — A connection is a peer: the container is the grant (design arc)
